title: SLO decompaction pipeline and correlated-noise filtering for burn-rate precision
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Our burn-rate alerts are noisy during cross-service incidents because SLO buckets are colocated and the aggregate signal masks which downstream service or cache layer is driving the spike. This causes oncall thrash and long time-to-mitigation. Goal: Build a decompaction pipeline that splits aggregate SLO time-series into orthogonal contributor signals (service, region, request-path, model-size) and apply correlated-noise filtering to suppress alerts that are caused by known background churn (deployments, tracing sampling shifts, probe storms). The feature should reduce false positive burn-rate pages by >= 40% in the first month without increasing time-to-detect real degradations.
implementation_plan: Instrument lightweight attribution tags at the ingress layer (route_id, model_variant, tenant_tier) and pipe through the trace-hook enrichment change proposed in ENG-31415.

Create an aggregator stage in the observability pipeline that performs 'decompaction': from aggregate SLO series produce per-dimension series using streaming group-by and cardinality capping to avoid explosion.

Implement correlated-noise detector: a statistical model (windowed pearson + robust MAD) that identifies simultaneous uplift across unrelated groups and labels it as systemic noise unless accompanied by elevated error-rates or latency gradients.

Add burn-rate policy adapter to alerting engine: when a candidate burn-rate alert is raised, consult decompaction outputs and correlated-noise verdict to decide: page, create a ticket, or suppress with auto-resolve window.
Provide a fallthrough 'force-page' flag for opt-in critical tenants and an audit log entry for every suppressed alert for post-mortem visibility.
Ship dashboards showing decompaction heatmaps and a suppression audit feed; initial dashboards under console -> Observability -> Decompaction.
Run a 2-week dark launch where suppression decisions are logged but not executed, collect precision/recall metrics, then ramp to active suppression for low-risk services.
Post-launch: iterate thresholds and add ML-derived signatures if needed (follow-up epic).
acceptance_criteria: Decompaction pipeline produces per-dimension SLO series for route_id, model_variant, and region with <5% data loss across a 7-day sustained window.
Correlated-noise detector achieves >=40% reduction in paged burn-rate false positives on staging historical replay (evaluation harness attached).
Suppression decisions are recorded to audit logs and surfaced in the new Decompaction -> Suppressions dashboard.
No increase in median time-to-detect for real degradations (measured across three canonical incidents) beyond 10% compared to baseline.
Configurable opt-out at tenant-level and force-page flag validated with SRE during rollout.
Docs updated: Confluence runbook describing tuning knobs, failure modes, and how to rollback suppression policy.
